s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on the right arm 2 months after initiation of immunotherapy
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Numerous eosinophils were present on biopsy
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

differentials: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome
per_call: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques

shortlist.label: Pembrolizumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving pembrolizumab, which is a known cause of skin rash

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is receiving ipilimumab, which is a known cause of skin rash

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of numerous eosinophils and perivascular inflammation support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of eosinophils and perivascular inflammation, although less likely given the lack of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship between the immunotherapy and the rash, and the presence of eosinophils on biopsy is consistent with an immune-mediated reaction

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic scale and no mention of other diagnostic features

rejected.label: Ipilimumab-induced rash
rejected.why: While possible, pembrolizumab is more commonly associated with rash as an immune-related adverse event

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: Biopsy findings are not specific for this condition and the clinical presentation is more consistent with a drug-induced rash

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: No systemic symptoms or other organ involvement reported, making this diagnosis less likely
